speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Members have made other suggestions to address concerns about housing delays and supply.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Louis Chua and Mr Gan Thiam Poh suggested building more flats with shorter waiting times.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Significant land and infrastructure preparation is needed before we can build BTO flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Where possible, we have brought forward our plans for land preparation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This allows us to launch flats with shorter waiting times.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will launch more such flats in future where we can.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Sale of Balance Flats, Open Booking of Flats are also flats with shorter waiting times.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But all these depend on whether sites are available.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For brownfield redevelopment, we may be delayed if, for example, existing users of land require more time to relocate or if existing services need to be diverted.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For greenfield sites, we need to carry out detailed environmental studies.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In fact, we have accelerated many of our plans in order to increase the BTO supply over the next two years.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: That is our priority, to meet the current strong demand.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Leader of the Opposition asked if we would also review the various HDB priority schemes and give absolute priority to certain groups.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Priority schemes allocate housing supply to meet the needs of a wide range of Singaporeans – to support marriage and parenthood aspirations of young couples, the desire to live with or close to parents or married children for mutual care and support, or the housing needs of our singles and seniors.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For each scheme, we set aside a certain proportion of flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Those who qualify for the scheme and are balloted within that quota are guaranteed the chance to select the flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Those who are balloted outside of the quota will be considered with the other applicants who do not qualify for the scheme.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In that sense, each priority scheme guarantees a certain number of flats for qualifying applicants and so, addresses different categories of households and families in Singapore who have needs.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But we cannot guarantee a flat for all the applicants in any one of these priority schemes for a particular launch because there may well be more applicants than there are flats set aside for each scheme.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It would mean that the other groups who do not qualify for that scheme would not get a chance to book a flat at all.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This could include singles, couples who do not have children and others.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We would also need to build a lot more flats and use a lot more land to meet this demand if done this way.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Instead, our approach is to strike a calibrated balance between the housing needs of different groups.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, contrary to the Leader of the Opposition's characterisation of the way in which we set aside our priority schemes, it is not one in which priority refers only to more chances but, rather, in trying to balance the needs of different groups, we provide absolute priority within certain quotas to ensure that one group does not then eat up the quotas and spaces for other groups.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As for putting up information on the application numbers under different priority schemes, HDB already provides the number of applications received for each project across the various household types for every town and flat type.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These figures are updated through the application period for each BTO and SBF exercise.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Applicants can refer to this information in deciding which project to apply to.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Besides managing current demand and supply, we also continue to enhance our housing policies.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Mariam Jaafar asked what we were doing to make public housing fairer and more inclusive.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also plan to build public rental flats in future PLH projects where possible.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Pritam Singh and Mr Louis Chua raised some concerns about the PLH model.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They have been raised by others, considered and addressed during our extensive public engagements.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But let me go through them again quickly.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Pritam Singh asked how we determine the subsidy recovery rate.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As we have explained, because PLH flats are in prime locations, we need to provide additional subsidies, on top of the usual BTO subsidies, to bring the price of the flat down to an affordable level for more Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Louis Chua suggested lowering the subsidy quantum at the point of sale.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: If we were to do that, it would just mean that only those with higher incomes or wealth can afford these flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is to be fair to the other BTO flat buyers who do not get these additional subsidies.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Taken together with the other measures, such as the 10-year MOP, disallowing of rental of whole flats and ring-fencing the pool of eligible buyers to those meeting the BTO eligibility conditions at the point of resale, among others, would help to mitigate excessive windfall gains.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Pritam Singh also asked how we determine which projects come under the PLH model and, if PLH might push up resale prices of neighbouring flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We look carefully at the attributes of each project, including expected selling prices, to decide if we should apply the PLH model.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As to whether neighbouring resale flats will see higher prices, this is unlikely as they are much older flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In any case, it will be another 15 years or so before PLH flats reach the resale market.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, we will keep studying and monitoring this.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Louis Chua asked why singles are not allowed to buy PLH flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To moderate resale prices, we require resale PLH buyers to meet BTO eligibility conditions, which are a set of criteria that most people are familiar with.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These criteria include singles who are part of larger households with caregiving responsibilities, say, they are buying a home with parents or with their siblings, if their parents are not around.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And these would apply mostly to older singles.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The PLH model is very new and we have only launched two projects.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will continue to monitor the response to PLH projects and review the parameters as part of our regular policy reviews.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Besides socioeconomic inclusiveness, we also want our public housing estates to reflect our society’s ethnic diversity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Ethnic Integration Policy (EIP) seeks to support that.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It enables people from different ethnic backgrounds to interact in their daily lives – around their homes, at the markets or hawker centres, in schools, in neighbourhood shops, in playgrounds and so on.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: That provides some of the conditions to foster tolerance and understanding and counteract the powerful social forces that tend to divide societies.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Without EIP, racial concentrations could be much higher in various parts of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, EIP remains relevant and important in promoting racial harmony and I am glad that we had established bipartisan consensus on this after our debate in this House last July.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are mindful that some flat owners may face difficulties selling their flats when the EIP limits are reached.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, some may have to lower their asking price or may take longer to sell their flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have been helping these families in different ways, such as by giving them more time to sell their flats and even waiving the EIP limits in exceptional circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But it is not sustainable to keep waiving the EIP limits, because this would erode the very objectives that EIP seeks to achieve.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Over the years, we have continued to receive feedback about the rough edges of EIP and suggestions on how to smoothen them from the public and Members of Parliament, including Ms Mariam Jaafar, Mr Chong Kee Hiong, Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Lim Biow Chuan, during this debate.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have said before that we would continue to study these options.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This complements existing forms of assistance that I have just articulated.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But those who are EIP-constrained and need to move out earlier due to extenuating circumstances can still apply to HDB for special consideration.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In assessing households for buyback assistance, we will consider the household’s specific circumstances, including how long the household has been EIP-constrained and whether they have marketed their flats consistently at reasonable prices.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In deciding how best to assist EIP-constrained flat owners, we had considered other suggestions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat suggested applying the EIP limits over a larger geographical area.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Pritam Singh had also previously suggested this.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But this could likely lead to over-concentration of particular ethnic groups at the local level, in specific blocks or neighbourhoods, rendering EIP less effective.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And when the limits are reached in larger geographical areas, significantly more flat owners will be constrained.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: At that point, HDB may have to waive the EIP limits in even more cases.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, this is not a viable long-term solution.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong and Mr Lim Biow Chuan suggested giving a grant to households which may have to sell their flats at a significantly lower price due to EIP.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have studied this in detail, but found that it would be difficult to implement in practice.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, it would be difficult to size the grant fairly.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: A fixed grant may undercompensate some sellers but overcompensate others.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Yet, a variable grant, say, a certain percentage of the transacted price, would give sellers with higher flat values more support in absolute terms, which might not seem fair to others.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is not a decision that we make lightly, because it requires significant Government resources.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But we believe it is the right thing to do, because EIP benefits all of us and helps to foster a more cohesive society.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: During our exchange in Parliament on EIP last year, he wanted data to understand what was unique about EIP-constrained neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I had said that we would look into what we could practically provide, given the large volume of data requested.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In our response to his two Parliamentary Questions, we had provided comprehensive figures, such as the number and proportion of blocks and neighbourhoods that have been constrained by the different EIP limits over the last 30 years as well as the areas corresponding to some of the neighbourhoods that were EIP-constrained in both 1990 and 2020.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: However, there are practical limitations to providing all the data sets requested.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For instance, he had requested the names of all EIP-constrained neighbourhoods from 1990 to 2020 – a 30-year period.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But there are no public maps or demarcated areas that we can make reference to.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, we did the next best thing and provided corresponding areas, but it would have been difficult to do so for all neighbourhoods without significantly compromising accuracy.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, where practical, we have and will continue to provide the information requested to further everyone’s understanding of the issue.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I think it is important to clarify this.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Next, we want to contribute to a more inclusive society by meeting the housing aspirations of low-income families that need more support.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin asked how we will help families in rental housing to own their own homes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our public rental housing system is not just about providing homes for lower-income citizens.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also want to provide integrated social support – in education, healthcare, training, employment and many other areas – to help them achieve stability and improve their situation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And that is what Community Link, or ComLink, is all about – to enable lower-income families with children to achieve stability, self-reliance and, ultimately, social mobility.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For those who are ready for home ownership, HDB’s Home ownership Support Team (HST) will guide them through their journey.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also provide financial support to make home ownership more affordable for these families.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First-timer families can benefit from the usual first-timer grants like the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (EHG), whereas for second-timer families with children, we introduced the Fresh Start Housing Scheme in 2016.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They can buy 2-room flats with a shorter lease, which are otherwise only available to seniors.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Families will also receive close support from a social service agency to ensure that they can sustain home ownership.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We want to give more support to these families who aspire to own a home again for their children to grow and develop.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, as the Finance Minister had announced in his Budget speech, we will enhance the Fresh Start Housing Scheme in two ways.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are doing so to provide these families with more housing options.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It is a substantial change that we are making in our housing policies, to support lower-income families and their children, as they seek to improve their lives.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My colleague, Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim, will share more details on our other efforts to uplift households living in rental flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As our population ages, we are also paying close attention to the needs of our seniors.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In particular, we are doing more to help seniors age-in-place while getting appropriate care.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We launched our very first Community Care Apartment, an assisted living pilot, in Bukit Batok last year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim will share more details on our plans to launch a second Community Care Apartment pilot and to work with the private sector to provide more assisted living options.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Members have suggested that we do more to support the housing needs of other groups, such as singles or those who prefer rental to home ownership.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My colleague, Senior Minister of State Sim Ann, will address some of these suggestions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann will also share more about how we are making our HDB estates more vibrant and liveable.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The sector was badly impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic and Members, such as Mr Henry Kwek, have asked about its progress.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Throughout this period, we have worked closely with the industry – not just on BTO projects, but also more widely across the sector to deal with the challenges that have come our way – from manpower shortages to cost increases and supply disruptions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We still hold regular meetings and site visits to understand the situation on the ground and to find a way forward.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are thankful for the close partnership with trade associations, companies and workers, as the sector recovers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Construction output has reached close to pre-COVID-19 levels and work is progressing steadily.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is more than five times the monthly average of 3,000 between May and October 2021, when travel restrictions were in place.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: While the Omicron variant has had an impact on firms, we are much better prepared this time around, after the difficult lessons we have learnt when the pandemic first struck.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will continue to monitor the situation carefully, because the sector is still under some stress.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Above all, the pandemic has reminded us how important it is for the sector to be resilient to shocks.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The sector remains heavily dependent on migrant workers to take up manpower-intensive jobs at construction sites.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, we need to step up our transformation of the sector, which we started when we launched the Construction Industry Transformation Map in 2017.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Together with our industry partners, we are determined to make a decisive change in how we do things in the sector.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will push on to improve the quality of our construction workforce and shift more towards productive work processes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To drive this transition, the Minister for Finance and the Minister for Manpower had earlier outlined the changes that we are making to our foreign workforce policies.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will make it easier for firms to hire workers for more productive and skilled work.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This means that firms will be able to hire fewer migrant workers per local worker.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Some might ask why we are making these changes when the industry is still recovering.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But it is precisely our painful experience from the pandemic that has shown us why these changes are necessary.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And as the sector recovers, we should seize this opportunity to fundamentally change how we design, build and maintain our city.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These foreign manpower moves should be looked at together with other efforts to raise productivity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, we have enhanced our buildability framework over the years to raise the standards for manpower-efficient designs and technologies.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And from April this year, all larger buildings must be designed in ways that require less manpower to construct.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This means that the industry should need fewer workers when the foreign workforce policies take effect from 2024.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong and Mr Henry Kwek have asked how we will support firms to digitalise and adopt productive technologies, such as Prefabricated Prefinished Volumetric Construction (PPVC).

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Indeed, this continues to be a key priority.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This year, to support firms and workers to be more productive, we will extend various schemes under the Construction Productivity and Capability Fund (CPCF).

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My colleague, Minister of State Tan Kiat How, will elaborate on this later.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will also push ahead with built environment sustainability to address climate change.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: During the Green Plan Joint Segment, I had spoken about the importance of greening our buildings.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling and Ms Mariam Jaafar asked if we will do more to reduce emissions in existing buildings.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Today, more than half of our buildings that are more than 20 years old have not been retrofitted and they lag behind newer buildings in terms of energy performance.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will do this by significantly enhancing our Green Mark Incentive Scheme for Existing Buildings.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The previous scheme supported retrofitting costs for more than 80 buildings and achieved more than 180 gigawatt hours in annual energy savings.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is equivalent to the annual energy consumption of close to 40,000 4-room flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Under the enhanced scheme, we will raise the minimum qualifying standard from Green Mark Gold to Green Mark Platinum and expand the scheme to include residential as well as light industrial buildings.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Building owners can choose the strategies and technologies that are most appropriate for their building.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, they can upgrade the cooling system, install solar panels or redesign spaces for natural ventilation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The grant amount will be based on the additional carbon abatement and Green Mark certification achieved, instead of the cost of works, as was used by the previous scheme.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will consult our industry partners on this before deciding.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Together, these efforts will help to enhance the productivity, sustainability and resilience of our built environment sector.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Transformation is never easy, but it also creates many exciting growth opportunities and we look forward to working with the industry on this.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Let us turn to another important priority: transforming Singapore into a City in Nature.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: During the Joint Segment on the Green Plan, I spoke about the progress that we have made.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Why are we striving to become a City in Nature?

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We face intense land-use pressures, as a city state.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We need to find space for all the things that a country needs, within the limits of our city-state – not just homes, community amenities, industries and offices, but also reservoirs, airports, seaports, military bases and all the other things that larger countries can site far outside their cities.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And amid these intense pressures, we also want to conserve our natural heritage.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To do this, we take a science-based approach – to understand the ecological value of our green spaces and identify the most important ones to conserve.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In some cases, this means retaining green spaces that were intended to be developed for other purposes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Last year, we also launched the Ecological Profiling Exercise (EPE), in partnership with experts and members from the nature community.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin asked for an update on this.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Based on the EPE’s findings, we are creating more ecological corridors between our core nature areas.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, we have found that the forests at the western half of Ulu Pandan are richer in biodiversity than its eastern half.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, we will safeguard a sizeable nature park there.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also found that the green networks around Toh Tuck, Maju and Clementi are important stepping stones between Bukit Timah Nature Reserve and the Southern Ridges.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, over the next few years, we will establish a Clementi Nature Corridor that runs through these green spaces, including the eventual nature park in western Ulu Pandan.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Beyond strengthening ecological connectivity, we also continue to expand our islandwide park connectivity networks, to give Singaporeans greater access to green spaces near their homes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In January, we launched the eastern half of Phase 1 of the Round Island Route.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Covering a total distance of 75 kilometres, this green connection makes the journey from Rower’s Bay to Berlayer Creek more seamless and accessible.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Prof Koh Lian Pin asked what more we can do to involve Singaporeans in nature conservation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Being a City in Nature is not just about our living environment.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It is about who we are as a people – how we respect nature, take care of it, steward it responsibly.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are encouraged by the strong support of our community partners.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Over 320,000 trees have been planted under the OneMillionTrees movement, involving over 30,000 members of the community.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Many volunteers have also helped restore and enhance our green spaces, through the Friends of the Park initiative.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And last December, through our City in Nature Conversations, we heard many thoughtful suggestions on how to advance our greening journey.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We invite Singaporeans to join us in realising our vision of a City in Nature and grow a greener, more liveable and sustainable home.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Besides stewarding our natural resources, we also want to safeguard our history and heritage.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As we look to the future, we must also remember our past.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our built heritage is important because it gives present and future generations a sense of place, identity and rootedness.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our built heritage has significant intangible value that we should safeguard.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Today, heritage conservation is an important consideration in our planning process.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When evaluating development proposals, URA works closely with the National Heritage Board (NHB) to determine the conservation merit of our buildings, consult relevant stakeholders and calibrate how to balance conservation with development.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Over the years, we have continued to refine our approach to safeguard our built heritage and expand our engagement efforts with the heritage community and key stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, we formalised constructive working relationships with the heritage community by setting up public-private-people partnerships like the Heritage and Identity Partnership (HIP) and NHB's Heritage Advisory Panel (HAP).

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These partnerships allow us to tap on their expertise upstream at the planning and design stages of developments to optimise how we conserve and celebrate our built heritage.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have been developing a structured framework to evaluate when and how additional heritage impact studies should be conducted as part of the planning process.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In 2018, URA, HDB and NHB commissioned NUS' Department of Architecture to pilot a large-scale detailed heritage study of the Old Police Academy.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Old Police Academy played an important role in the professional development of Police officers from the 1920s until 2005.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And since 2016, the Singapore Police Force (SPF), URA and HDB have been engaging the larger Police fraternity on how we could celebrate and sustain the heritage of the Old Police Academy.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The heritage study report was also published for public feedback last year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Members of the public who wrote in include a former trainee who shared his memories of the place.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: He suggested retaining certain roads and certain road names.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They will be meaningfully adapted for contemporary use.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For buildings and spaces which cannot be retained in their entirety, we will explore how to sustain their heritage significance in the design of the new housing estate.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: HDB and SPF have also formed a dedicated workgroup chaired by Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim with Police and heritage stakeholders and have started to discuss how to celebrate the rich heritage of the Old Police Academy.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The HIA will complement URA and NHB's existing processes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Findings will be shared, unless there are security or other concerns, and members of the public will be invited to give feedback.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Heritage communities and other stakeholders will continue to be engaged throughout the process.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We expect such detailed and in-depth HIAs to only be necessary for larger-scale public development projects in areas of rich and complex heritage significance.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For other projects, URA and NHB's existing processes remain adequate.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The implementation of the HIA framework marks an important milestone in the maturation of our heritage evaluation process and we will continue to refine this process along the way.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Keeping public housing affordable and accessible, transforming the built environment sector and growing Singapore into a City in Nature and safeguarding our built heritage – these are some of the key priorities that we are working on.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have to do all these, while meeting the evolving needs and aspirations of Singaporeans, all within the confines of our small city state.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But it is also due to tight constraints like these that the most creative and resourceful ideas are born.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As part of our Long-Term Plan Review, we are reaching out to Singaporeans from all walks of life, to hear their goals and dreams and aspirations for our future city.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My colleague Senior Minister of State Sim Ann will give an update on this.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We hope all Singaporeans will walk with us on this journey, as we build a better city, together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Feedback on municipal issues has indeed significantly increased with the onset of COVID-19 as Singaporeans spend more time at home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This has spurred us to find new ways to work and to forge stronger partnerships with the public on issues which the Government alone cannot fully resolve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MSO will work with our partners to make progress in three areas: increasing productivity of municipal services; improving processes for better user experience; and forging stronger community partnerships to holistically address complex neighbourhood issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our key goal is to deliver resident-centric services in an efficient and seamless manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The OneService app has been a useful platform to achieve this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is, today, a one-stop neighbourhood platform with many functions, beyond reporting feedback.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is the result of MSO constantly enhancing the OneService app to meet residents' evolving needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For instance, to help residents plan around potential disamenities and inconveniences, residents can now refer to the "Happenings" feature for information on HDB-approved renovation works at their blocks and will soon be able to check the crowd levels at public libraries should they wish to find alternative locations to study or to work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Residents can also access the "Book Facilities" feature to perform end-to-end contactless booking and payment for the use of common areas and facilities, such as multipurpose halls and void decks in their estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are also finding ways to deliver better services with the pilot of integrated municipal operations in Tampines town and have commenced ground operations last month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Next, I will speak about improving user experience, as mentioned by Miss Cheryl Chan and Mr Yip Hon Weng.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Most are straightforward cases that can be resolved within a week, but some complex cases can be long-drawn, especially where investigations or neighbours' cooperation are required.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Case owner agencies, currently, have the flexibility to decide how to close cases, be they straightforward or complex.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MSO is working with our partners to improve the handling of municipal feedback, in terms of how they should close the feedback loop for the different types of cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For straightforward cases that involve only one agency and where concrete actions can be taken to fully resolve the case, agencies should close the feedback loop only upon complete resolution of the case.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For complex cases, agencies should close the feedback loop only after explaining to the feedback provider the actions taken or the intended action plan, as well as provide an estimated timeline.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have implemented two corresponding changes in the OneService app.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, we have differentiated the status of cases since May 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With differentiated case status, residents have a more accurate understanding of the status of their case and can be assured that unresolved cases continue to be worked on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will also continue to make our OneService e-services more accessible by introducing them on more digital platforms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the second half of the year, residents will be able to submit feedback using the LifeSG app, in addition to the OneService app.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In time, more of our digital offerings will be available on LifeSG so that residents who are currently not users of the OneService app can also enjoy our e-services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Together, we hope that tighter collaboration in the delivery of municipal services will bring greater convenience and satisfaction to residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked for an update on new technical methods to lower the costs of the Lift Upgrading Programme, or LUP, for HDB flats without direct lift access.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over the years, HDB has adopted innovative technical solutions, such as machine-room-less elevators and bubble lifts to provide direct lift access for such flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There remains about 150 blocks where it is not possible to implement LUP due to prohibitive costs or existing technical and site constraints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue to explore how to bring down LUP costs, as well as alternatives to LUP, such as powered stair climbers for wheelchair users.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Lift access Housing Grant is also available to help residents with urgent mobility or medical needs to move to another flat with direct lift access.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Several Members – Miss Cheryl Chan, Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Baey Yam Keng asked about MSO's efforts to address neighbourhood disamenities that arise due to differences in social norms or behavioural issues, such as the cluttering of common spaces, high-rise littering, bird feeding and noise from neighbours, given that work-from-home will remain an option for many people in the longer term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Due to demand, the operating hours of the work booths at Trivelis Residents' Network centre have also been extended to late evenings and the weekends.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue to monitor the outcomes of the pilot after a year and consider scaling it up if there is good demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Group-buy activities support small businesses and promote interaction among residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But when large quantities of goods are delivered to an estate and redistributed to individual buyers, there could be inconveniences, such as cluttering of goods at the common corridor and blocking of passageways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We would like to identify win-win solutions so that residents can continue to engage in group buying and support small businesses while minimising inconvenience to others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Members of the AfA will consist of stakeholders, such as group-buy hosts, grassroots leaders and potential solution providers from the private sector, to explore better ways of facilitating the delivery, storage and distribution of group-buy items, such as making use of HDB void decks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, we will continue to focus on shaping positive social norms to mitigate neighbourhood disamenities due to human behaviour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is an upstream measure and one of many that needs to be put in place to holistically address the management of community disputes, as explained by Minister Edwin Tong during MinLaw’s COS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Lim Biow Chuan rightly highlighted that neighbourhood noise is a complex issue to resolve and can cause significant tension and unhappiness between neighbours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MSO and MCCY are exploring various ways to tackle this issue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Community Advisory Panel (CAP) will consist of representatives from the community who have the relevant experience and expertise in managing municipal issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The "community norms" developed by the CAP will help neighbours to better communicate with one another, as well as serve as a useful "benchmark" and reference for our public advisories, and to facilitate mediation and decision-making at the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We hope to establish CAP soon and for the panel to submit its recommendations by the end of the year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MSO is also working with MCCY on how agencies would enforce against neighbourhood noise using these "community norms" as a reference and Minister Edwin Tong will share on this aspect during MCCY’s COS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With this feature, concerned residents can directly connect persons-in-need to social agencies, without risking over-exposing them on social media.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I thus encourage everyone to use "Help Neighbour".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I would now like to address Mr Xie Yao Quan’s query about HDB’s plans to keep our heartland shops vibrant and sustainable, amid the rise in online shopping and changing consumer habits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our heartland shops must do well if our neighbourhoods are to remain vibrant and endearing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Beyond serving the day-to-day needs of residents, heartland shops reflect the distinctive character and identity of our neighbourhoods, provide spaces for residents to meet and interact and serve as a social glue for the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our heartlands can also be incubators for budding entrepreneurs and exciting new business ideas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Since 2007, HDB co-funds physical upgrading works and promotional activities through the Revitalisation of Shops scheme to improve the shopping experience for our residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB also partners Enterprise Singapore to encourage our heartland retailers to modernise their operations and embrace digitalisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To ensure our heartland shops stay relevant and vibrant, HDB and Enterprise Singapore are further engaging the public through the Heartland Shops Study to understand what Singaporeans value most in the heartlands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Since October last year, we have engaged over 2,400 residents, business owners and shop employees through surveys, interviews and focus group discussions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I joined one of these public engagements earlier in February and was excited to hear ideas on how we can shape the heartland retail scene, while preserving its cultural and social value.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Together with HDB, we will thus explore ways to better curate the trades at our neighbourhood centres, taking into consideration the attributes that residents and businesses have told us they value and also better support the digitalisation and business sustainability of these shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I encourage all Singaporeans to participate in the online survey for the Heartland Shops Study which is available on the REACH website until the end of this month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We embarked on the review last year to refresh our long-term land use plans for the next 50 years and beyond.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have conducted regular reviews of our long-term plans since the first Concept Plan in 1971.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Key infrastructure outcomes of the 1971 Concept Plan include Changi Airport and our current MRT lines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We found that Singaporeans aspire towards four key broad outcomes for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, a sustainable Singapore – a city where we can grow in an environmentally responsible way, especially in light of climate change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister Desmond Lee covered our sustainability efforts extensively earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, an inclusive Singapore – a city where we can meet the diverse needs of our people and foster social cohesion and harmony.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim will share more on how we are supporting our vulnerable citizens and forging community partnerships later.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Third, an adaptable and resilient Singapore – a city where we can adapt nimbly to disruptions and seize emerging opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MSE colleagues yesterday provided an update of our efforts to build a more resilient Singapore, such as our coastal protection plans to combat rising sea levels, our development of weather-resilient water sources through desalination and the transformation of our used water network with the Deep Tunnel Sewerage System.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Fourth, a distinctive and endearing Singapore – a city that we are proud to call our home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister Desmond Lee shared earlier about how we will strengthen the character and identity of our city by safeguarding our built heritage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Since October last year, we have followed up and facilitated in-depth discussions with more than 1,000 participants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also tapped on discussion forums and webinars involving more than 7,000 participants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We discussed how we could achieve the four desired outcomes and how we should balance the trade-offs required.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Some of them were quite imaginative, like using our canals and waterways as transport networks, or building floating or underground housing apartments to overcome our land constraints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The public engagement is still ongoing and will culminate in an exhibition in the middle of this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We encourage Singaporeans to continue contributing their ideas and views.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: While not all of them are feasible today, they are harbingers of the future possibilities we need to keep in mind.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: On public housing specifically, Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin and Mr Louis Chua asked about expanding public rental housing to cater to more groups of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Leader of the Opposition and Miss Rachel Ong also asked about housing access for singles and families with non-citizens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For the rental housing that HDB offers, our emphasis is on providing highly-subsidised rental flats to those who have no other housing options, such as those with financial difficulties, as well as first-timer families who have challenges renting from the market while waiting for their booked flats to be completed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Rent-To-Buy arrangements may serve a purpose in societies where there are significant gaps between home ownership aspirations and affordability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In Singapore, we design our public housing financing policy to minimise this gap.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have also been expanding housing options and grants over the years for households of singles and families with non-citizens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For instance, single buyers have access to housing grants and can buy smaller BTO units in non-mature estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: While our overall housing policy continues to support families, we, nevertheless, recognise the home ownership aspirations of singles and, particularly, the circumstances of singles who are also caregivers and seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are very mindful of their concerns and will continue to study ways to assist them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With limited land, we will have to consider the trade-offs and resources needed whenever we make policy changes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For instance, whenever we raise the income ceiling or liberalise eligibility criteria for public housing – for example, by lowering the age limit, demand will go up and we will need to make sure we have the land and the resources to meet such demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: While our current priority is to catch up on the delays caused by the pandemic which Minister Desmond Lee has spoken about, we recognise that the needs and aspirations of Singaporeans are changing, including those who are single or have non-citizen spouses and will continue to study how best to extend more support to them as the situation stabilises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As we carefully balance trade-offs and hedge against future uncertainties, innovation and human ingenuity offers opportunities for us to overcome our constraints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister Desmond Lee earlier spoke about enhancements to our Cities of Tomorrow (CoT) R&D programme to fulfil our vision of a more sustainable, liveable and resilient Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The research efforts under the CoT programme also allow us to tap on advancements in big-data analytics and social science research to aid our urban planning and design.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In Mandarin):   Singaporeans are spending more time at home since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As a result, feedback on municipal issues has significantly increased in the last two years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Among these, neighbourhood issues, such as noise from neighbours, cluttering of common spaces, high-rise littering and bird feeding, are more difficult to resolve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MSO will work with Government agencies, residents and communities to collectively address these neighbourhood issues and maintain a pleasant living environment, in two ways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, we are collaborating with the business community and the public to harness innovative ideas and bring practical solutions to residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The pilot will last for a year, after which we will consider scaling it up to other areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: PA and HDB will also be co-leading an Alliance for Action (AfA) to study practical solutions to better facilitate group-buy activities in HDB estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Group-buy activities are getting more popular these days, supporting small businesses and promoting interaction among residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, it can also cause inconveniences to some residents, such as cluttering of goods at the common corridor and blocking of passageways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The AfA will invite stakeholders, such as group-buy hosts, grassroots leaders and private companies, to identify better solutions together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, as an upstream measure, we will continue to focus on shaping positive social norms to mitigate neighbourhood disamenities due to human behaviour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The CAP will consist of representatives from the community who have the relevant experience and expertise in managing municipal issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We hope to establish CAP soon and invite the public to jointly discuss and develop a set of “community norms” regarding neighbourhood noise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, defining what is deemed as unacceptable or uncivil behaviour, as well as what residents should do to reduce noise disturbances to their neighbours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Let us work together to create a better living environment for all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In English): We will continue to work closely with our partners to maintain high service standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To emerge stronger as a society, we need residents and communities to work together towards our shared goal of a better living environment for all.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: But the past two years have also shown us that Singaporeans share common aspirations for a caring and inclusive society and want to contribute to making Singapore a better home for all.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, I will share more about our efforts to support different groups of citizens, especially those who may require more assistance, and create vibrant places in partnership with the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: First, on those staying in public rental flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Some Singaporeans face more challenges than others in life.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For those who are lower-income or more vulnerable, providing highly subsidised rental housing is an important first step.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With shelter, they have a safe space to come home to, a stable foundation upon which they can regroup and stabilise.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Louis Ng spoke about giving more assurance to single unwed parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We understand the anxiety that families may face when their housing arrangements are uncertain.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: All rental flat applicants may contact HDB at any point for updates on their applications.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: HDB will also prioritise flat allocations for those with urgent housing needs as far as possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Beyond housing, those in public rental may also be grappling with other challenges: health issues, family conflict, employment troubles and more.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: So, public rental housing is not just a shelter; it is a home that comes with social support, to help our rental tenants bounce back stronger.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, under Community Link, or ComLink, HDB and many other agencies work together to support families with children living in public rental housing.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: ComLink proactively reaches out to families to understand their unique challenges and aspirations, provides close case support through befriending and action planning, and works with community partners and volunteers to offer customised programmes and services that meet families' needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Through ComLink, we hope to empower families to regain stability, become self-reliant and, eventually, achieve social mobility.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: On Mr Chong Kee Hiong's concerns regarding larger families in public rental flats, families may request for a 2-room flat if there are three or more persons.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Multi-generation families that can form two family units may also apply for two flats and HDB will try to ensure that both flats are located near each other.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We also work closely with MSF and Family Service Centres at selected ComLink sites to offer 3-room rental flats, coupled with social support, to larger families with children.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With a limited supply of 3-room flats, however, we are only able to offer them to a small number of families on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Like Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin, we hope to help rental tenants achieve their aspirations to own their homes.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: HDB has a dedicated team of officers, the Home ownership Support Team, who will guide rental tenants on their journey towards home ownership.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin asked how families will be identified.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Home ownership Support Team estimates the housing budget of households, based on their income and CPF information that they last shared with HDB.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They help families make sense of available housing schemes and grants, provide practical tips and advice, and walk families through the processes of buying a flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Families can also benefit from generous housing grants when they purchase a flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Second-timers can tap on the $15,000 Step-Up CPF Housing Grant.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are also enhancing the Fresh Start Housing Scheme this year, as Minister Desmond Lee shared earlier, to help second-timer families with young children in public rental to own a home again.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These grants ensure that public housing remains affordable and accessible, especially to lower-income families.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Another 2,200 or so households have also booked a flat and are waiting for their new homes to be ready.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I encourage all rental families to aspire and work towards home ownership.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Government and community will support and complement your efforts, as you work towards better lives for yourselves and your loved ones.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For low-income singles under the Joint Singles Scheme, or JSS, Mr Lim Biow Chuan and Mr Chong Kee Hiong spoke about the unique challenges they face when it comes to finding or getting along with their flatmates.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We understand these concerns and are continually exploring ways to address them.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Last year, I shared that HDB will pilot the JSS Operator-Run model.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Under this model, singles can apply for public rental without finding a flatmate first and an appointed social service agency will manage the flats and flat-sharing arrangements.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We currently have two sites, in Bedok North and Buangkok Crescent, which are managed by Good News Community Services.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: So far, about 90 tenants have confirmed their tenancy and some have already moved in with the flatmates whom they were matched with.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I visited the site at Bedok North recently and was encouraged to see that tenants were, generally, able to get along.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I also spoke with the operator, who plays a critical role in this model.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They help tenants adjust to living together, address other challenges that tenants might face and foster a living environment that is comfortable and supportive.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Plans are underway for a third site in Bukit Batok and we will continue to monitor the effectiveness of this model, to see how it can be improved to better meet the needs of singles.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Henry Kwek, Mr Xie Yao Quan and Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin asked about our efforts to help seniors age in place, including our plans to provide assisted living options.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As Mr Henry Kwek and Mr Yip Hon Weng mentioned, this is something that the PAP Seniors Group also cares about.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We understand that many seniors prefer to age in environments they are familiar with, surrounded by family and neighbours they can depend on.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: So, we have made extra efforts to provide senior-friendly homes and estates.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Within homes, seniors can tap on HDB's Enhancement for Active Seniors programme, or EASE, to install senior-friendly features for mobility and comfort.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Together with other agencies, we will continue to refine the enhancements offered under EASE, to help seniors age independently in their own homes.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At the town level, our physical infrastructure also offers an inclusive and user-friendly living environment for all ages.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have features like gentle-sloping ramps for barrier-free accessibility, and pictograms on directional signages to aid wayfinding.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Earlier this year, we also formed a pilot community partnership in Boon Lay, called "Our Accessible City @ Boon Lay Neighbourhood".

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Together with the local community, including seniors and persons with disabilities, we will study how to address accessibility gaps in the HDB heartlands.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We also intend to form a similar partnership in Nee Soon Central later on.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Beyond infrastructural features, we work with agencies to provide amenities and services in HDB towns so that seniors can meet their needs easily.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, at the integrated developments at Kampung Admiralty and Yew Tee, senior-friendly housing is co-located conveniently with healthcare, commercial and community facilities under one roof.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In each HDB estate, HDB also sets aside spaces for social service agencies to offer services to residents onsite.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Depending on residents' demographic profile and needs, these services could include home and day care services or befriending services, which provide support for seniors to age in place.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We want to offer a spectrum of housing options to meet the aspirations of seniors to age autonomously and gracefully in place.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In particular, we want to meet the aspirations of our senior population for assisted living housing typologies that integrate housing and care services together.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Hence, MND, HDB and MOH worked together to develop the Community Care Apartments (CCA).

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Affordably priced, it combines senior-friendly housing with care services that can be customised according to seniors’ needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It also offers communal spaces and social programming for seniors to interact and stay engaged with the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There will also be common facilities, such as roof gardens, fitness stations and community living rooms, to promote social interactions among all residents.
