speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This second site is situated within the Health District at Queenstown, where HDB, NUS, healthcare partners like NUHS and local grassroots organisations are piloting new strategies to create a built environment that promotes a healthy lifestyle and active and healthy ageing.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Queenstown also has the Alexandra Hospital, which will allow medical and healthcare services to be seamlessly incorporated into the care model for residents.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: HDB will share more specific site details later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will also launch a site at Parry Avenue for sale by public tender later this year, for a private assisted living facility, to give seniors even more assisted living options.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The facility may accommodate about 300 to 400 seniors.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I invite prospective tenderers to propose innovative assisted living models to help our seniors age gracefully within the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We look forward to partnering the private sector to co-create new assisted living housing products that will further enhance the quality of life for our ageing population.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Beyond seniors, other segments of our population also have diverse needs and aspirations.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, Mr Louis Ng asked about catering more lactation rooms in buildings to better support working mothers.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Code on Accessibility which buildings have to meet, by default, includes a requirement to provide lactation rooms.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Only certain types of buildings, like offices, are currently not required to provide lactation rooms if they are below a certain size, in consideration of practical space limitations.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Nonetheless, the Government encourages building owners and occupants to go beyond the requirements of the Code to cater to the needs of building users.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For instance, businesses suffered when footfall fell, due to border closures and other safe management measures.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To rejuvenate these heritage precincts, the Government takes a participatory approach on the ground – to actively engage and respond to local communities and find a more resilient and sustainable way forward.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This includes working with stakeholders to mitigate gentrification risks and allow older tenants and newer stallholders to exist alongside each other in a seamless and complementary way.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In Kampong Gelam specifically, local businesses, institutions, landlords and residents had come together to form the Kampong Gelam Alliance, or KGA, to collectively look into various long-term issues concerning the area.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To encourage greater interest in the rich heritage that Kampong Gelam offers, the alliance recently worked with URA, LTA and students from LASALLE College of the Arts to put up posters detailing Kampong Gelam’s storied history around Bugis MRT Station.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I have taken on the role as advisor to this alliance and will work closely with existing and new community stakeholders to support their efforts for the area.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Together, we hope to preserve the heritage that makes Kampong Gelam distinctive and, at the same time, refresh it so that it remains relevant for future generations.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I also invite Singaporeans to share your visions for Kampong Gelam when KGA engages the community and public later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Your ideas will guide our efforts to keep Kampong Gelam alive as a centre of community, culture, heritage and enterprise.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Through partnership platforms like the pilot Business Improvement District programme, URA also works closely with local stakeholders to transform other neighbourhoods into vibrant and attractive destinations.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They are making good progress and we will continue to collaborate with private sector and community partners to enliven neighbourhoods across Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In Malay):   Last week, Mr Faisal Manap spoke about Malay families living in public rental flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We understand that families in public rental have the same aspirations as other families.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They want a home where they hope to build a bright future for their families.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: But many of them are also dealing with multiple challenges, such as health issues, family conflict and employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: So, in public rental housing, the Government gives them both a physical home as well as social support.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We take a holistic and coordinated approach to uplift families in rental flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Through initiatives like ComLink and Project DIAN, HDB works closely with other social agencies and community partners to identify families’ needs and provide the support they need to achieve self-reliance.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: When families are ready to own a home of their own, they will also receive the help they need.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are ramping up our public housing supply to provide more affordable housing options for Singaporeans, including those from the Malay community.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, families can receive personalised guidance from HDB’s Home ownership Support Team, that is, HST, who will advise them on their housing options and guide them through the flat purchase process.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Families can also benefit from significant housing subsidies and grants, such as the CPF Housing Grant and Step-Up CPF Housing Grant.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We hope these enhancements will make it easier for rental families to have a better living environment for their loved ones.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: If you would like to find out more about how you can work towards home ownership, HDB will be happy to assist.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Kampong Gelam is an important area to the Malay/Muslim and wider Singapore community.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: So, we want to work hand in hand with the local stakeholders and other citizens, to keep it vibrant and preserve its culture and heritage.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I recently took on the role as advisor to the Kampong Gelam Alliance, that is, KGA, which unites local stakeholders, such as businesses, residents and institutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Together, we will work closely to address local issues and ensure that Kampong Gelam continues to be a place that we hold dear.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I also invite Singaporeans to share your ideas with us at an engagement session organised by KGA later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In English): Mdm Chairperson, to conclude, let me reassure everyone that we are committed to supporting vulnerable citizens, meeting the diverse needs of all Singaporeans, and creating vibrant and endearing spaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: And we will do so in close partnership with citizens and the community, to make sure that Singapore continues to be a place that all of us can truly call home.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Over the past two years, COVID-19 has posed significant challenges for the BE sector, as shared by Mr Henry Kwek and others before him.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The support has been made available to all our construction firms, including sub-contractors.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Government has also recently announced the extension of the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme (TBLP) and the Enterprise Financing Scheme – Project Loan to support firms’ cash flow needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Notwithstanding the support available to contractors, we understand that some Town Councils are facing higher tender prices, as raised by Mr Gerald Giam.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This issue was also raised by Ms Tin Pei Ling and Ms Ng Ling Ling last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Giam suggested that HDB temporarily increase its Neighbourhood Renewal Programme (NRP) grants.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Upgrading projects, such as the NRP, remain important to rejuvenate older HDB estates to benefit our residents.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As I shared with Ms Tin then, our overall fiscal situation remains tight and I encourage Town Councils to start by reviewing the scope of your projects and reduce upgrading items if possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Nonetheless, we are in regular discussions with all Town Councils and we will continue to monitor the situation closely.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Giam also suggested that HDB provides materials price protection for contractors of town improvement projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: HDB does provide such price protection for its BTO contractors.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This includes offering contractors the option of guaranteed protection against steel price fluctuations, where HDB will pay their contractors, if the price of steel exceeds the price that is protected by HDB.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Another example is stipulating a fixed quantity of concreting material that HDB will supply at the point of tender closure.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: However, the contracts for town improvement projects are between Town Councils and their own contractors, and it is up to each Town Council to decide whether to adopt this approach.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: HDB understands that Town Councils, generally, do not do so as their projects are not as complex or as extensive as BTO projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Giam also suggested that MND explores measures to strengthen confidence within the construction sector and for parties to better manage risk.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have been doing so and the public sector is taking the lead.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: First, we made clear the grounds for the Extension of Time caused by pandemics.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Third, BCA has also worked with Government Procuring Entities (GPEs) to provide a provisional sum for anticipated cost items during the pandemic, such as swab tests, in their new tenders.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: With this, contractors need not price these costs into their tender bids.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These practices minimise the need for contractors to buffer significant additional cost in their bids to cater for uncertainty.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Henry Kwek asked about the inflow of foreign manpower for the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: He also asked how the Government can continue to work with our trade associations to support the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Government has worked closely with the industry to facilitate the inflow of migrant workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Our industry partners, including trade associations like the Singapore Contractors Association Limited or SCAL, spearheaded efforts to implement a tightened end-to-end process to bring in migrant workers in a safe manner.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Workers can also enter Singapore via MOM's Work Pass Holder General Lane.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The streamlined process will help the CMP sectors accelerate the entry of necessary workers for ongoing projects, alleviate the labour shortage while building greater resilience in the workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: At the same time, we must accelerate our push for transformation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We started this journey back in 2017 and have worked with stakeholders to put together the Construction Industry Transformation Map or ITM.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: There are three key outcomes: achieving automation through Design for Manufacturing and Assembly or DfMA; enhancing digitalisation through Integrated Digital Delivery or IDD; and promoting sustainability through green buildings.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Through DfMA, we are moving construction work off-site into a controlled factory environment, where building modules are prefabricated before assembly onsite, achieving higher labour productivity and safer worksites.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have been pushing for DfMA adoption in the industry over the years.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong spoke about raising the adoption of Prefabricated Prefinished Volumetric Construction (PPVC), which is a form of DfMA.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: It is well suited for residential and hotel developments.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Our PPVC adoption rate is, currently, about 20% by GFA.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: It has remained at around this level during the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This is because while labour costs have risen, the cost of imported PPVC materials has also risen.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will continue to encourage PPVC adoption through the Government Land Sales (GLS) programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For instance, we require PPVC adoption for suitable residential and hotel GLS sites, including HDB executive condominium developments.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are also putting in place greater modularisation and standardisation requirements under the Buildability Framework to lower costs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: However, PPVC may not be suitable for all developments, especially developments with site constraints or smaller developments without economies of scale.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: But let me reassure the Member that we will continue to push for the wider adoption of DfMA, including PPVC, wherever possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Through IDD, stakeholders across the building lifecycle from upstream design to downstream facilities management can collaborate more seamlessly through digital platforms.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: And we have greened more than 49% of our buildings by GFA under the Singapore Green Building Masterplan.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: But we will need to accelerate our transformation efforts in light of the lessons learnt from COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: At the same time, the operating environment for the built environment sector is rapidly changing.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Against this backdrop, we have begun refreshing our transformation plans under the Future Economy Council (FEC) Urban Systems (US) Cluster Sub-Committee.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Co-chaired by Mr Liam Wee Sin from UOL Group Limited and myself, we have been engaging stakeholders across the sector – developers, builders, consultants, contractors and facilities managers.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will share more details later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: However, to kickstart the next bound of transformation, we encourage our built environment firms to tap on various incentive schemes in making the transition.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: PIP has helped many firms, including SMEs, adopt DfMA and IDD technologies that have made construction work more productive.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Under PIP, firms can benefit from support of up to 70% of the cost of adopting solutions like DfMA and IDD technologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Second, we will extend the iBuildSG Scholarship and Sponsorship scheme until March 2023.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This scheme has been very helpful in enabling our built environment firms to attract young talents.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Firms can also continue to apply for the Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG), which co-funds up to 70% of the cost of adopting off-the-shelf digital solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Taken together, these Construction Productivity and Capability Fund (CPCF) schemes will support firms to transform and build the pipeline of local talent and be better prepared for the foreign manpower tightening moves that would be implemented in 2024.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In addition to transforming the way we build, we need to change the way we maintain our buildings through facilities management (FM).

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: By 2025, more than 50% of our buildings will be above 30 years old.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Given the twin pressures of ageing buildings and rising manpower costs, we will need to press on with our efforts to transform the FM industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan asked what steps we will take to accelerate the FM transformation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We agree with Miss Cheryl Chan that there is a need to do more to encourage the adoption of new technologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In particular, FM firms can harness efficiencies from managing different FM services on an integrated platform and aggregating FM services across many different buildings.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I recently visited CBRE, a firm that provides FM services to office buildings, industrial spaces and laboratories.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Through its integrated Vantage Analytics platform, CBRE is able to virtually manage its entire portfolio of buildings for its full suite of FM services, including security, cleaning and energy management.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: CBRE's services have helped its clients, including public sector agencies, attain significant cost savings.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This is what we call integrated and aggregated FM.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Both service buyers and providers play key roles in the adoption of advanced technologies, as a part of integrated and aggregated FM.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This includes smart FM technologies that enable predictive maintenance and investing in the infrastructure for data and analytics, as both Ms Tin Pei Ling and Miss Cheryl Chan had pointed out.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: And we also agree with Miss Cheryl Chan that service buyers, including our Town Councils, should look at adopting outcome-based contracts that can facilitate advanced technologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: At the same time, service providers will need to level up their capabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: That said, the adoption of integrated and aggregated FM remains nascent, especially for existing buildings, given the high retrofitting costs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We plan to fund around 10 to 15 projects across different building typologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This will establish the business case for wider adoption.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I seek the strong support of our building owners and FM firms to explore integrated and aggregated FM for your operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In addition, we will continue to leverage R&D to push the boundaries for automation, digitalisation and sustainability through innovation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These innovations include customisable robotic systems for on-site assembly and off-site construction, and building designs that facilitate the use of robotic solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are also investing in next-generation construction techniques and technologies, such as 3D concrete printing (3D CP), to complement the adoption of robotics in raising productivity.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Chairman, I have detailed how we will transform the built environment sector to be more manpower-lean and resilient.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: But we will need to complement these efforts with a resolute focus on jobs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Henry Kwek and Mr Cheng Hsing Yao had asked how we would attract more Singaporeans to join this sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Our ongoing transformation efforts have helped us to create good jobs for locals in the areas of DfMA engineering and digital delivery.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I recently met Mr Teh Ming Xuan, a planning engineer working for Kimly Construction whose studies were supported by a joint iBuildSG scholarship between BCA and Kimly.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Through an internship with Kimly, Ming Xuan became interested in how construction can be radically transformed via DfMA and IDD.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: He now provides technical support in these areas, working on the implementation of digital platforms and prefabrication to raise construction productivity.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: He also contributes to Kimly's R&D efforts in advanced robotics and automation and actively explores how new innovations can be deployed for Kimly's projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In addition to the iBuildSG Scholarship and Sponsorship scheme, we have put in place a multi-pronged approach to attract and upskill talent.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: First, we will continue to work closely with our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) to engage our students on built environment careers through the iBuildSG Club.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are also working with IHLs to incorporate emerging skillsets in DfMA, IDD and green buildings into their curriculum.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: And we will undertake further initiatives to better retain our Polytechnic and ITE graduates.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will partner our IHLs to put in place more work-study programmes and provide meaningful internships for our students.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Second, we will support our mid-career entrants through putting together more Career Conversion Programmes (CCPs), which provide on-the-job training to help our mid-career entrants pick up new skills more quickly.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For instance, we have managed to train 94 individuals as Building Information Modelling (BIM) modellers in the past three years.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Third, we will continue to work closely with trade associations on accreditation schemes to raise standards within the BE sector and encourage more firms to adopt the Built Environment Skills Framework.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For example, I recently met Boustead Projects, a firm that has actively invested in training its employees to keep pace with industry transformation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Over the years, Boustead has leveraged BIM to deliver quality construction projects, through digital visualisation of building designs, documentation and cost estimation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This has allowed Boustead to develop its own in-house training programmes to train its employees in these skillsets.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In fact, Boustead has curated training programmes, in partnership with NTUC Learning Hub, BCA Academy and IHLs as a SkillsFuture Queen Bee, for employees of SMEs across the BE sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As we embark on the next bound of industry transformation, we will also need to update our existing initiatives.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This is why we are embarking on a Jobs Transformation Map (JTM) study for the BE sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Many of our existing schemes adopt a broad-based approach to workforce development.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: But there is a need to be more targeted in our approach and tailor our initiatives to grow in-demand jobs for the next bound of industry transformation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: (In Mandarin):   Over the past two years, COVID-19 has posed significant challenges for the BE sector, such as the increase in construction costs, supply chain disruptions and manpower shortages.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Government has provided comprehensive support to help the sector tide over the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: With the support provided, and the resilience and actions of our industry partners, we continue to see signs of recovery from COVID-19 for the BE sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Construction output has recovered to close to pre-COVID-19 levels.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: That said, the Government continues to monitor the situation carefully and could introduce further support measures if necessary.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Above all, the pandemic has reminded us how important it is for the sector to be resilient to shocks.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will need to accelerate our push for transformation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In particular, we will need to become more productive and reduce our heavy dependence on migrant workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In this regard, the Government will continue to support our firms on this journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will extend various schemes under the Construction Productivity and Capability Fund.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I encourage firms to make full use of our schemes.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: If we work together, we can create a resilient, sustainable and liveable built environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: (In English): Across our collective efforts to transform the BE sector, the Government will take the lead through our public sector projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We also remain committed to working hand in hand with our industry partners on charting the path ahead in the new normal.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Together, we can create a future-ready built environment and emerge stronger from COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Gerald Giam had asked about our efforts to manage bird pest issues in housing estates.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: NParks is also carrying out research to understand the ecology of birds, including how their reproductive biology and factors, such as food availability, can affect their population.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: And NParks has been sharing best practices with our Town Councils.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: That said, trapping birds and moving them to another location, as suggested by Mr Gerald Giam, is not a feasible approach.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will be transferring the problem to another group of residents.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: A more sustainable approach will be keeping our public and common areas clean and free of food waste.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In this regard, we will need the assistance of all our Town Councils and the public.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Louis Ng had also raised the issue of cat ownership in HDB flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As part of our broader efforts to improve standards in the pet sector, we have been engaging stakeholders on a range of issues, such as improving dog rehoming and adoption processes, raising standards of pet boarders and breeders.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: And we are reviewing and will continue to review pet ownership policies to ensure that they balance the needs of different segments of the community, including pet lovers and those who might have concerns about disamenities that may arise.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are considering this issue from various angles, including enhancing our strategies for the management of both pet cats and stray cats, to effectively manage the overall population of cats in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: I have a clarification for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: The issue I highlighted for MND's consideration is not really one between neighbours.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Rather, the issue is disamenities caused mostly by non-residents and we know they are non-residents because we patrol the sky gardens or roof gardens nightly.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: I note that a committee looking into disputes will be formed and I hope that the gating proposal that I made can be seriously considered, studied and, hopefully, implemented.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: HDB has been working together with Ms Joan Pereira and her team on the management of the sky gardens that she has talked about.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We understand where Ms Joan Pereira is coming from and will continue to work with her to look for sustainable solutions.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But more importantly, does it suggest from HDB's data that, for the more recent BTO exercises, this rise is actually warranted?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: We recently heard feedback from residents, as I am sure Minister would also have received from newly married couples and couples with children that they are repeatedly unsuccessful in their BTO applications.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, I think that clarity would be quite helpful.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I welcome the announcement of the buyback option for EIP-constrained households, so as to make things fairer for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But I note that this position that was announced today was actually the original last resort solution that was put out by then MND Minister, Mr S Dhanabalan, when he introduced the policy in the late 1980s.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can I confirm if HDB had applied this last resort earlier and, if not, why had it not applied it earlier, because the Minister in the late 1980s already said that this was a last resort option to buy the property from the affected EIP household?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Actually, I had asked a written question in July about how many times HDB had purchased an EIP-constrained flat and the reply actually was specific to voluntarily surrendered flats.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: That was the reply that the Ministry gave.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, I am not sure whether it was an answer to the same thing, whether the flat was actually purchased by HDB in the first instance, as HDB would have committed to do if there were EIP-related constraints, or whether it had not purchased any EIP-affected flat previously.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, has this actually been done before, because the policy was already announced earlier?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I acknowledge the Minister's point about the difficulty in coming up with a map which is consistent over time.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I asked the question because of the previous EIP-related question I filed.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The Ministry actually provided the five-yearly interval data.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, naturally, I asked whether that data could be further clarified in those five-yearly intervals, but I note the Minister's point.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But let me first talk about the priority schemes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I said in the speech that we provide data for individual BTO launches.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, let us, say, we launch in a particular area, like Tengah.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Each BTO launch, we put out a couple of locations and we say what kinds of housing typologies are available in each location and we specify the application rates for each project, at each launch on a daily basis.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That will, in our view, give potential home buyers the most practical and meaningful data that they will then be able to use in determining whether to make an application for that flat in that location or not.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, we provide that data, not only for the location, but for each housing typology.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We think that the data we put out needs to be practical and meaningful for flat buyers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Of course, those who apply for balance flats or flats in mature estates, particularly where the attributes are very attractive, demand will, naturally, be high across all the possible priority schemes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, for each launch, for each site, we have allocated quotas for each group, for example, for married children and their parents; for multi-generation families, where relevant; for the Tenant Priority Scheme.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For ASSIST, you should be a widowed or divorced second-timer with children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The application rates will vary for a variety of reasons.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: One, of course, because of the current pandemic situation where people are concerned about housing delays and more people put in applications earlier or based on location and attributes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some are extremely attractive and lots of people will apply for them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, in terms of the data we put out, we want it to be practical and useful for home buyers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And whether the Married Child Priority Scheme can be raised, in a way when you talk about "X" number of dwelling units or units in any particular launch in any particular location, it is almost like a zero-sum game because, you have, say, 1,000 units and you have a certain percentage for married children, a certain percentage for other groups, for seniors, based on typology, if you increase one group in terms of quota, then you must eat into other groups and, ultimately, the second-timers will be squeezed out.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, we want to make sure that we provide a balance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: HDB looks at all the data, not just for individual sites, but overall launches across the years, and also looks at long-term demographic trends and data, to decide whether we need to make any adjustments to the quotas and priority schemes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Therefore, we keep a very close eye on this.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On EIP, when EIP was introduced in 1989, the resale market was really nascent.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The number of resale transactions back then pales in comparison with the resale market that we see today.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, all the way to the year 2000, if my memory serves me right, people could surrender their flats to HDB for any reason and not just because of EIP.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And it took a period of time for the resale market to become mature in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And then, we put in the various measures that we put in place that I have articulated before – waiving EIP on exceptional basis; giving home buyers more time to sell if they feel the constraint and so on.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, that is my response to the Leader of the Opposition's question, if I got him right, in terms of when the buyback option was last used.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Then, the Leader of the Opposition had asked the question about the written Parliamentary Question for data and I had explained that we received a request for significant data-sets by the Leader of the Opposition.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We had endeavoured to give the data that we were able to provide.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And for the second Parliamentary Question that there were constraints with regard to neighbourhoods, neighbourhood names, boundaries and so on, it is all in the reply.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And if the Leader of the Opposition looks at the Hansard and he is not satisfied about the response in any way and needs more clarification, we welcome him to put forward a further request and we will clarify.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On singles, Senior Minister of State Sim Ann had explained that we want to be responsive to the evolving aspirations of all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A number of years ago, singles could not buy HDB BTO flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But keeping an eye on how society is evolving and that more Singaporeans are either choosing to remain single as a matter of choice or becoming single because of circumstance – they have caregiving obligations and so on – that group is growing and we wanted to provide for them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Hence, we made the decision to provide BTO eligibility for singles quite a number of years ago, but, certainly, less than 10 years ago.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And along the way, we have adjusted the grants and made more flexibilities to accommodate singles and to provide for them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But every group that has eligibility for HDB BTOs, there will always be constraints.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Leader of the Opposition earlier said that he wanted the priorities to be real priorities, not a gamble – you have high priority but, actually, it is really just a ballot and a gamble and more chances.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, the reality that the Leader of the Opposition now recognises also is that we will have to make adjustments along the way, but also balance the needs of different groups for it.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: With respect to my last point about eligibility for singles, I take the Minister's point that there are zero-sum realities to think about here.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But I also wish to come back to the point that the Minister made earlier about the number of flats that HDB is prepared to construct from 2021 to 2025.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I think the number was up to 100,000.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: In view of what I shared in my cut about the latest population census and the number of singles that has gone up from the age groups 25 to 29 and 30 to 34, has that information prompted a change in HDB's thinking about its options for singles – which I acknowledge there were not any previously, and these have now been introduced – but in view of new information that is coming online, through the census as I explained, is there some scope to include the building of more flats for singles, for example, within that timeline the Minister has shared?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The census makes clear the social demographic trends in Singapore, including that of singles or even of delayed marriage and parenthood.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But this is not something that is news to us.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As both the Senior Minister of State Sim Ann and myself have said, our priorities are to make sure that we deliver the flats that people are waiting for and also address the significant demand from newly-formed households as well as nuclearising households.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, in a paper that the Workers' Party itself put out in 2019, they cited data from, I believe it is the Department of Statistics, showing the family size or the median family size per household, coming down very sharply.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And that, of course, comes through in the form of greater demand, both for married households, households with seniors, singles and so on.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But as Senior Minister of State Sim Ann said, both sides of the House, we all want to provide for Singaporeans and meet as many needs as we can and to help as many people achieve their home ownership aspirations as possible.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we live in a situation where both land and resources pose real constraints.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And, in fact, if neither land nor resources were constrained, we want to meet everyone's needs all the time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we will have to make priorities for different groups, based on income, nationality, number of chances they got owning a home based on their family obligations and then make some adjustments, helping those who may need more help and giving them more support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, that is where we are and we continue to look at the needs of Singaporeans and the housing options that they have.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Can I ask Senior Minister of State Sim Ann about this Community Advisory Panel?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Who is expected to be on this panel?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Would members of the public be involved in this panel?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Also, what about other issues, like second-hand smoke and hoarding?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Would Senior Minister of State Sim Ann be able to clarify that?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We are starting with noise because, amongst the different kinds of neighbour disputes that I have raised, which have their roots in human behaviour, neighbour noise is the most numerous and we would like to gain more experience from using this Community Advisory Panel to form these norms and then work in concert with enhanced community dispute resolution mechanisms and gain some experience from that before we apply it to other forms of neighbour disputes.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: The first is regarding the BTO cut that I had filed.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: It is really whether or not we could set aside a minimum target percentage of the flats.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: So, instead of the Build-to-Order (BTO) process, we have one which is build-ahead-of-order, considering that we do have a very significant demand and supply imbalance in the market today, with very high over-subscription rates for the BTO flats.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: The second is in relation to resale subsidies and ensuring affordability.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: So, what is it that the Ministry would be looking into to ensure that it is not only the better-off who can afford a flat in these places?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Member asked if more shorter waiting time flats can be built.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The answer is that we are doing everything we can to do so.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But that requires us to not just do land preparation and that work is very significant – you have to clear encumbrances, do land preparation, you may need to clear the land, provide the services, the roads.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, where does this land come from to meet all these needs, or growing needs?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To which, the Workers' Party would like to add more demand, which we will look at.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we will have to take land from greenfield sites.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And the Workers' Party has said, "Please keep as much greenery as possible".

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But some of these sites, we will have to use.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, please support when the studies are out.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some of them are brownfield sites, which means they have been cleared of their previous use and the land is ready to be developed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But often, brownfield sites are still being used – whether they are used for businesses and industry or for nurseries, farming or retail or whatever, and we have to give the user of the land the time to be able to clear out and then we take over.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And if there is a delay in that, that will affect our land preparation, that will affect our launch, that may cause delay to our housing plan.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, to plan for a BTO programme requires many years of planning ahead of time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And, wherever possible, we will advance it in order to allow shorter waiting time flats to be launched.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, one is coming up, starting this month.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I look forward to residents who need immediate housing to apply for those.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As for affordability of resale flats, there are certain areas which are very popular, the flats' resale prices are higher.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But part of it is in the last year or so, because of COVID-19, because of concerns about construction delays, coupled with the ongoing socio-demographic trend of household formation and smaller households, had resulted in greater demand for resale flats; particularly in some areas which are very popular.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we also have put in place the Prime Location Public Housing flats to ensure that, in some very prime locations, eventually, when they become resold on the market and became resale flats themselves, we have enough mechanisms and levers to try to ensure that they remain affordable, not just at first launch, but, over time.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: (In Mandarin):   I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State what are some of HDB's considerations in considering the profile of shops that it would prioritise in an area.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: (In Mandarin):   I would like to thank Mr Gan Thiam Poh for his question.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: With regard to the features of heartland shops, we are now conducting a public consultation exercise.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: According to the feedback we have received from the public consultation so far, they have a few unique features.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Some participants have shared that heartland shops should provide essential goods and services for residents and blend in with the spirit and ambience of the estate.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: They also hope to see more specialty shops and heritage shops in the heartlands and that the heartland shops will continue to operate and retain their local identity and connection.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: At the same time, there are others who wish to see more innovative shops that can offer residents a fresh shopping experience.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In general, most of the participants from the public consultation were of the view that there should be active curation and management of goods and services offered by the heartland shops.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We will continue with the consultations based on the feedback received.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: After collating and analysing all feedback, we will craft a plan to enhance the shopping experience in the heartlands.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: On the flip side of my question, the group that, due to EIP, cannot rent or buy flats nearer to their parents, is there something that the Ministry is also thinking to do for them?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: Great to hear about the grants for retrofits being extended to residential buildings, too.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: But, of course, HDB is the primary volume driver here.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: Can the Minister also give an update on the roadmap for HDB to retrofit its large base of buildings, as well as new buildings, to become greener?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: I say this knowing that it has a lot of socioeconomic impacts; I do not take it lightly, but it would be great if the Minister could share something on the roadmap.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In the joint segment on the Green Plan, I had shared briefly about efforts that we will be undertaking under HDB Green Towns.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We aim to put solar panels on as many HDB rooftops as possible, subject to studies like loading, technical considerations, whether it gets adequate exposure to the sun and so on.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And for new BTOs, to make every HDB rooftop solar panel-ready, so that when the SolarNova contracts come their way, they are ready to be fitted out with solar panels.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The pneumatic waste management system under the HDB Green print in both Ang Mo Kio and Yuhua has shown that they are best done for new BTOs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Likewise, for the rainwater harvesting pilot in Yuhua.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But for existing BTO flats, we are piloting cool paints on the surfaces of existing HDB blocks to reflect more heat away and to make the ambient environment in the homes more liveable and, in that regard, help families manage the cost of keeping their homes cool at the hottest times of the day or year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And, of course, making every effort to green our HDB towns as much as possible and, hence, the OneMillionTrees, getting people heavily involved in HDB towns to plant as many trees in the town as possible.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, these are just some of the many things we are doing to retrofit, or to help our existing estates to be greener and more sustainable.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, HDB has now one more tool in the toolkit to help some of these families address their personal pain points, in order for society as a whole in Singapore to understand and support the policy of EIP, to keep our estates ethnically diverse.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Member's point is about the reverse, people who want to buy a resale flat in an area that is near their parents' homes, but are facing a constraint because the seller cannot sell to them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In those cases again, I would say, put an appeal through.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Let HDB take a look because it works both ways.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They cannot buy, seller also wants to sell.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And then, we will have a look globally at both the buyer and seller's situation.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: I got one clarification in regard to EIP and it is addressed to the Minister.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: First of all, I thank the Minister for the explicit move on the EIP.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: It has been a long time coming to help families or individuals who cannot sell.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: My first clarification is about the fair offer.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: In what way can the Minister reassure sellers involved in this EIP appeal, on a case-by-case basis, and residents have suggested this as well, as in a buyback from HDB?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: But how can the Minister reassure that the price will not be too low when the valuation comes in and what is the valuation level that will be coming up?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: The second question is, sometimes, the seller could be seniors who stay in some of these old mature flats and they stay alone.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: How can HDB help them to compile these documents for submission?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: I know property agents may be involved, but, in some ways, how can we inform some of these senior sellers with regard to documentation?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Because it looks quite onerous in terms of collecting listings for six months and all that.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Certainly, we cannot match the highest possible resale prices in the area.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we will make sure the offer is fair, the seller will be told and given time to consider.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: He can, of course, write to HDB if he feels that he disagrees with the quantum, but that is an offer that HDB makes after taking in inputs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On seniors living alone and if they face these difficulties, please ask them to approach the HDB branch office and we will do what we can to support them if they face difficulties carrying out the process in order to avail themselves of some of these support mechanisms.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I have two clarifications for Minister of State Tan Kiat How.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Today, NTUC has formed Company Training Committees (CTCs) with some Facilities Management (FM) companies.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Through these CTCs, we are working very closely with the companies to transform their business operations and upscale their workers, achieving win-win outcomes.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: So, my first clarification is whether MND and BCA will work with NTUC and Building and Allied Trades' Union (BATU), that is, our building, construction and timber industries employees' union, to reach out to more FM companies to establish CTCs with them?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: My second clarification is whether the FM sector, both employers as well as workers, could benefit from adopting Progressive Wage Model (PWM) with its wage and skills ladders, so that we can better attract, retain and develop local professionals in this growing sector?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Mr Chairman, Mr Melvin Yong had two clarifications.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I will answer the first one about working with NTUC and, specifically, BATU, in terms of upskilling and raising the level of professionalism, as well as wage and career progression for our FM workers.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The answer is, certainly, yes, we are happy to work together with NTUC, as well as our partners in BATU to do so.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In fact, this is something we are working very closely on with all partners: industry partners, companies, employers as well as our union leaders.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Specifically, on the modality of CTCs, it is one modality that we work closely with the union leaders and companies on.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Broadly speaking, I would say that we encourage the FM and the MA workers to go for training and accreditation to raise their professionalism and improve their competencies.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Because that is the sustainable way for wage progression and career pathways in both sectors.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And we are very heartened that many companies and workers have come on board many of the training programmes conducted either by BCA Academy or our trade associations, including the Singapore International Facility Management Association (SIFMA), the Association of Property and Facility Managers (APFM) and the Association of Strata Managers (ASM).

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, we are working together and we welcome a tripartite approach.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: To the Member's second question about the PWM within the FM sector, I understand that the NTUC friends are working very closely with MOM.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The Member has raised a proposal to look at the PWM for workers in the strata management sector and we are working very closely with MOM to look at the scope, as well as the merits of the issue.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We look forward to continue working with our NTUC colleagues on this.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: Two clarifications: can services in the Community Care Apartments (CCAs) be extended to seniors living in existing HDB estates?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: And two: why is a first-timer family not eligible for the Fresh Start Housing Scheme?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Member for the questions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: CCA is a new concept and we need to evaluate the pilot to see how it helps in the physical and socioemotional well-being of the seniors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: That said, today if you look at MOH, they also have services that look after the frail, for example, home and day care.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the same time, for those who need social support, we have the befrienders.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As we move forward, there will be a levelling up of the elder care centres to see how these can better serve as a point of contact for seniors in every community, providing active ageing, befriending and many more services where they can be a point of contact.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But we are encouraged by the support and also the responses from the public about CCA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will closely study its impact and we really want to make it work, so that we can give opportunities for our seniors to age-in-place.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: I have the following clarifications: would these flats be added to the PPHS or Public Rental Scheme to meet rental demand from singles or families in the eligible minority ethnic groups?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: My second clarification is for Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: Could the Minister of State provide an update on the current situation of EIP-constrained owners?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: All flats that are bought back, we are likely to prioritise them for home ownership, put subsidies and put them out as balance flats to meet housing demand.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But depending on circumstances and on location, we may also consider them for PPHS or other uses, subject, of course, to EIP.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For the number of appeals, we have seen the number of appeals going down over the years, from 2019 to today.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, with these changes, we hope we can support the home owners better.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Chairman, because I am also aware of the Guillotine Time, so, I shall file my clarifications in subsequent Parliamentary Questions (PQs) instead.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Would you like me to withdraw my amendment?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Yes, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: I want to begin by thanking Minister Desmond Lee, Second Minister Indranee, whom we miss but I am sure she has been preparing for this COS as well, Senior Minister of State Sim Ann, Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State Tan Kiat How and the entire MND team who have been working very hard to address all the varying topics that we have raised.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Housing policies and land planning topics are complex for the fact that they have a lot of stakeholders that they interact with and also because they address genuine needs on a day-to-day basis.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: By recognising this, the Ministry has been trying its very best to help many people on the ground, based on all the feedback that we have received.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: I hope that we can continue refining the policies over time, in order to make sure that we can strengthen the schemes that are available, so that it really helps people.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Last but not least, it is important that we continue engaging citizens and partners to be able to shape the future Singapore, so that we can truly have a sustainable, resilient and liveable city and, together, we can build a home for all.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Chairman, with that, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
